headline: GOLD ENTERS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL 10-DAY WINDOW OF 2026 — CPI SEPT 11 THEN FOMC SEPT 16 SET THE DIRECTION
snippet: Gold consolidates near $4,420–4,440 entering the most consequential 10 trading days of 2026. The August CPI print on September 11 and the FOMC decision on September 15–16 frame a two-way binary: CME FedWatch puts a rate-hike probability at 59.9%, the highest since January. A hot CPI risks a test of the $4,136 support that held through the July lows; a soft print could ignite a breakout attempt toward $4,700+. Gold ended last week down 1.28% at $4,420 after August nonfarm payrolls blew out at 162,000 — more than double the 56,000 consensus — though analysts note prior inflation trends suggest the number may not lock in a hike. The week of September 7 begins with ADP private payrolls, PPI, and University of Michigan sentiment data, all of which will influence the FOMC calculus before the September 11 CPI closes the pre-meeting data window.

headline: ROLLS-ROYCE SMR PLANTS EUROPE'S FIRST SMR TURBINES AT SIEMENS NEWCASTLE — GWYNDOD WALES REACTORS TAKE INDUSTRIAL FORM
snippet: Siemens Energy announced September 4 that its historic CA Parsons Works facility in Newcastle, UK — which built the turbine for Calder Hall, the world's first commercial nuclear power plant, in 1956 — will manufacture high-pressure steam turbines and valve casings for Rolls-Royce SMR's first three small modular reactors at the Gwyndod site on Anglesey in North Wales. The contract marks the first time SMR turbines have been manufactured anywhere in Europe and is expected to create 550 jobs in northeast England. UK Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh attended the September 4 announcement. Three SMRs at Gwyndod carry a combined capacity of approximately 1,080 MWe and will require a sustained uranium fuel supply from first criticality through a 60-year operating life — a structural, long-duration demand signal for the uranium market.

headline: U.S.-SAUDI CIVIL NUCLEAR DEAL ALLOWS 20% URANIUM ENRICHMENT — PROLIFERATION ALARM RINGS AS NEW SOVEREIGN DEMAND PIPELINE OPENS
snippet: The civil nuclear cooperation agreement finalised between the Trump administration and Saudi Arabia this week includes a provision allowing uranium enrichment of up to 20% — classified as high-assay low-enriched uranium — pending joint feasibility studies on economics and nonproliferation safeguards within two years. Arms control researchers at the Middlebury Institute and Carnegie Endowment immediately raised proliferation concerns, noting that 20% enrichment clears roughly 90% of the technical work required to produce weapons-grade material. For uranium investors, the structural signal is unambiguously bullish: Saudi Arabia has publicly targeted 17 GWe of nuclear capacity by 2040, a buildout comparable to France's entire reactor fleet, requiring a multi-decade uranium fuel purchasing programme. If the enrichment clause survives Congressional scrutiny, it opens a Saudi domestic enrichment capability that could further tighten the global uranium supply picture.

headline: KENORLAND/CENTERRA DRILLS 204.34 g/t AU AT WESTERN WABIGOON — MAIDEN PROGRAM PROVES SHEAR-HOSTED GOLD SYSTEM IN NW ONTARIO
snippet: Kenorland Minerals (TSXV: KLD) reported September 3 the results of its maiden 4,089-metre, nine-hole diamond drill program at the Western Wabigoon Project in northwestern Ontario, held under option with Centerra Gold (TSX: CG). Gold mineralization was intersected in 8 of 9 holes, confirming a shear-hosted, hydrothermal gold system along the tested W2 target strike — the same style that defines prolific Archean lode gold deposits in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt. The standout intercept reached 204.34 g/t Au over 1.05 metres within broader envelopes of 37.75 metres at 0.30 g/t Au and 23.90 metres at 0.25 g/t Au. Centerra can earn up to 70% of the project by funding staged exploration through to a preliminary economic assessment. With gold near $4,420/oz and major producers starved of high-grade ounces, a new Archean gold discovery in Ontario at these grades will command attention on the next drill program.

headline: CPM GROUP ADVISES STANDING ASIDE ON GOLD THROUGH FOMC BINARY — OCTOBER CONTRACT RANGE TARGET: $4,320–$4,670
snippet: CPM Group published a September 4 trade advisory on the October 2026 Comex gold contract recommending investors stand aside through the coming 10-day FOMC binary rather than adding exposure at maximum uncertainty. The group sets an initial target price range of $4,320–$4,670 with the timeframe September 7–16. CPM acknowledges the structural bullish case for gold — sovereign central bank buying, fiscal deficit financing, debasement concerns — but argues that a near-60% probability of a rate hike and the potential for a sharp one-day move on CPI or payrolls data (gold fell 1.28% in a single session on the September 5 NFP beat) justifies patience. The firm maintains a medium-term bullish outlook and emphasises that any pullback toward $4,136–$4,200 would represent a strong accumulation zone for long-term positioning.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS DRILLS 83.8m AT 1.31 g/t AuEq AT TOMBSTONE — ARIZONA OXIDE GOLD ZONE REACHES 1,250 METRES OF CONTINUOUS STRIKE
snippet: Aztec Minerals (TSXV: AZT / OTCQB: AZZTF) reported September 2 that five new RC holes at the North Extension target at its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona returned exceptional oxide gold-silver mineralization. Best hole TR26-41 returned 83.8 metres of 0.90 g/t Au and 22.61 g/t Ag (1.31 g/t AuEq), including 7.6 metres of 6.97 g/t Au and 75.42 g/t Ag (8.34 g/t AuEq). The new holes extend the Contention mineralized system by 255 metres, pushing the continuously drilled strike to over 1,250 metres — an area where all holes remain in mineralization with no barren intersection recorded. Assays are pending for nine further holes (TR26-45 to TR26-53), two of which are collared north of TR26-43 along the trend. Tombstone's oxide gold-silver mineralization is heap-leach amenable, providing a low-capex development pathway rare among junior explorers.

headline: NdPr MAGNET COMPLEX FALLS AS A BLOCK FOR FIRST TIME SINCE MAY — NOVEMBER 10 CHINA EXPORT BAN EXPIRY THE SINGLE BIGGEST CATALYST LEFT IN 2026
snippet: The September 2026 rare earth market update shows the NdPr magnet complex — neodymium, praseodymium, and NdPr oxide alloy — fell together as a correlated block for the first time since May, suggesting speculative positioning rather than fundamental demand is the current price driver. The overall rare earth basket finished August with an average change of +0.31% and a median of +0.22%, with germanium leading at +10.04% and scandium posting the steepest decline at -7.36%. The most critical single variable for the remainder of 2026 is now November 10: that is the expiry date of China's one-year suspension of enhanced rare earth export controls — agreed at the Xi-Trump summit in December 2025. The suspension covered extraterritorial enforcement and expanded technology restrictions; China's core April 2025 licensing regime on seven rare earth categories has remained fully enforced throughout the suspension period and is widely expected to resume in full — potentially stricter — from November 11.

headline: ANTIMONY IS NOW A SECURITY COMMODITY — WESTERN GOVERNMENTS BET BILLIONS AS EUROPEAN PRICE HITS $23K/T, A 44% PREMIUM OVER CHINA
snippet: Crux Investor's September 2026 analysis documents how antimony has undergone a structural reclassification from industrial commodity to security commodity following China's September 2024 export licensing regime and its December 2024 ban on US exports. Antimony prices surged from roughly $12,000/tonne pre-controls to over $60,000 by early 2026 before retreating; today the European spot price sits at approximately $23,000/tonne — a 44% premium over China's domestic price near $15,940/tonne, reflecting the enduring friction of China's export licensing regime. The US Department of Defense has committed over $59 million to Perpetua Resources' Stibnite Gold-Antimony project in Idaho; Australia has pledged A$1.2 billion for its Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve with antimony as a priority metal. For junior mining investors, any project carrying meaningful stibnite or gold-antimony content now trades with a strategic premium — and the discount between junior market caps and replacement cost has rarely been wider.

headline: LITHIUM HOLDS $152K/T AS CATL JIANXIAWO MINE RESUMES — BATTERY METALS RECOVERY TRACK INTACT DESPITE AUGUST VOLATILITY
snippet: Lithium carbonate traded at $151,988 per tonne on September 5, stabilizing above the late-August trough of CNY 140,000 per tonne as two supply developments reinforced the recovery narrative. CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Sichuan — one of the world's largest hard-rock lithium operations — cleared security permits and resumed activity after a prolonged suspension, while Mineral Resources' Bald Hill mine in Western Australia continues to ramp production following its May restart (first spodumene concentrate produced July, 370 jobs created). Core Lithium's Finniss project in the Northern Territory has also restarted. Analysts note that the 2026 price recovery — up over 100% from 2024-2025 lows — is increasingly driven by stationary energy storage demand rather than EV demand, a shift that broadens and stabilizes the demand profile and reduces exposure to EV cycle volatility.

headline: GOLD SWOT SEPT 4: PALLADIUM LEADS PRECIOUS METALS HIGHER ON WEAK JOBS CLAIMS DATA — GDX RESISTANCE BREAKOUT PERSISTS
snippet: This week's Gold SWOT analysis (September 4, 2026) documents a notable technical divergence: major gold miners in the GDX have broken through significant resistance levels that gold itself has not yet cleared — a setup historically associated with miners leading the metal by approximately one month. Palladium led the precious metals complex on the week's weaker-than-expected September 4 initial jobless claims data, a signal that industrial and hedge demand is returning broadly to the group. The SWOT identifies gold's key strengths as central bank buying and structural fiscal deficits; key weaknesses as the 60% FOMC rate-hike probability and a strengthening US dollar post-payrolls; key opportunities as the September 11 CPI and the September 16 FOMC resolution; and the key threat as a prolonged higher-for-longer rate environment should August CPI surprise to the upside.

headline: SELLOFF OR BREAKOUT? CHRIS VERMEULEN'S SEPTEMBER GOLD TECHNICAL SETUP — $4,500 IS THE PIVOT, $4,136 THE FLOOR TO WATCH
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen (Sprott Money, September 2026) identifies $4,500 as the key pivot level determining whether September becomes a bullish continuation or a corrective episode for gold. Gold gained 10.5% in August and silver 14.9% in a powerful recovery off the July oversold lows; the September 5 NFP-driven pullback to $4,420 constitutes a short-term breakdown below the $4,450 support. Vermeulen's upside target is $4,700+; his downside risk scenario is a test of $4,136 support if CPI prints hot on September 11. He notes two bullish structural factors that override short-term rate noise: (1) gold miners' seasonal strength window — historically late June through late September — remains open; and (2) the August US Treasury announcement of its first steps toward Yield Curve Control represents what Vermeulen calls 'the single most bullish development possible for gold in 2026.' Position sizing cautiously into the FOMC binary, he advises, rather than swinging large in either direction.
